source.title: Who's Actually Paying? Measuring AI Agent Payments Onchain
source.license: not_verified; selected numeric facts and original-source link only

scope.end: not precisely stated in cited text; publication 2026-09-09
scope.measurement: settlements through known x402 facilitators, not all agent payments

screens: exclude bulk flows concentrated in one or two payers
exclude sellers with fewer than ten distinct buyers
publisher_method.permissive_model: facilitator-broadcast payments, sub-dollar average and variable prices
publisher_method.strict_model: also sustained across months and either ERC-8004 registration or payments to more than one seller

caveats: The low/high figures are heuristic model classifications, NOT statistical confidence limits, verified autonomous agents or verified distinct buyers.
The raw and screened totals are rounded research estimates; derived figures are conditional arithmetic, not independently audited settlements.
Monthly agent-like USD 5k–11k is the researcher's separate rough description, not a monthly rate inferred from cumulative totals.
TRM's thresholds may exclude genuine single-purpose agents or include scripted automation; on-chain agency cannot be proven from settlement alone.
Not comparable as a common cohort to x402stats, x402 List, x402 Lens or nohumans.directory rolling windows.
No AgentMine paying customers, revenue, realized fee capture, buyer willingness to pay, variable costs or procurement supplier savings are established.

implications.generic_transaction_fee_exchange: Do not estimate an addressable AgentMine fee pool from gross x402 protocol flow; verify recurring independently paying buyers and controllable routing.
implications.supplier_growth_saas: Not validated by on-chain protocol totals.
implications.lost_demand_intelligence: Searches and wallet activity still do not prove unmet paid needs.
implications.opt_in_rfq: Needs consented request/fulfillment outcomes and unit economics before monetization.
